fusion_ranked_evidence.title: First person gets new experimental vaccine for Ebola - BBC
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: ​​The first volunteer in the world - a 37-year-old UK man called Ed Hunt - has received an experimental vaccine against the Ebola virus. Hunt said he wanted to help after seeing news reports of the deadly Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo. ​​The vaccine, designed using the same technology as one of the UK's Covid vaccines, was given in Oxford where scientists developed it in just eight weeks. ​​He told the BBC what motivated him to take part: "I had wanted to volunteer for the Covid vaccine trial but was unable to because of work commitments. "The aim of the phase one clinical study is to look for the safety of the vaccine, and also to see if we're getting a strong immune response that could be protective against the Bundibugyo species of Ebola.". ​​There are four vaccines in development against the Bundibugyo species which has triggered the outbreak, but this is the first to enter human trials.
